title: Pilot operational readout - egress fallback & kernel compatibility
next_steps: Redwood to share kernel rollback playbook by 2027-02-25
StratusMed to provide sample egress traffic profile by 2027-02-28
Schedule bench run of canary model variant with reduced KV cache on 2027-03-01
action_items: Marco Diaz: prepare kernel rollback checklist and postmortem stub - due 2027-02-25
Ethan Cole: export last 72h egress metrics and top 20 endpoints - due 2027-02-28

summary: Mid-pilot sync focused on a recent kernel upgrade that increased tail latency for long-context calls. Team discussed temporary fallback routing, egress shaping to customer VPC, and next steps for conservative rollout with telemetry hooks. Security and audit requirements were clarified for Private deployment. Agreed to run a controlled canary and share rollback playbook.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-24
Start: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 32 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (CTO - StratusMed), Ethan Cole (NetOps), Marta Ruiz (Security)

[00:00] Lena Park: thanks everyone for joining on short notice, quick note, sorry if audio is weird, i'm on a train so apologies. we want to run through the last 48 hours of the pilot after the kernel patch, and get alignment on fallback routing and egress shaping. marco, do you want to kick off with the telemetry readout?
[00:22] Marco Diaz: yeah sure, i'll share screen afterwards, but quick summary first. after we pushed kernel v1.12.4 to the private nodes two nights ago, we saw a 6 to 12% increase in p95 token latency on long-context generative calls, largely when kv cache hit ratios drop below ~65%. short contexts unaffected. the CPU on the host stayed flat so it's likely a kernel-level scheduling interplay with our continuous batching path.
[00:45] Priya Sharma: when you say long-context, do you mean >1024 tokens or a certain window? our LLM usage for chart summarization hits 1.5k on average.
[00:58] Marco Diaz: exactly, 1.2k-2k sequences are where we observed the tail blips. the 99th pushed some calls over the 200ms SLA threshold we had hoped to keep.
[01:15] Ethan Cole: that matched what we saw from our side, we noticed spikes in egress retransmits around the same timestamps, not sure if related but worth flagging.
[01:24] Marta Ruiz: security question first, did that kernel change affect any of the KMS interactions or the audit pipeline? we need to make sure key rotations and audit flows weren't interrupted.
[01:35] Marco Diaz: no regression in KMS calls we can see; keys still fetch fine, audit events were ingested but with slightly delayed batching in our telemetry collector. nothing lost.
[01:45] Lena Park: great, thanks. high level plan options: 1) rollback kernel on the affected canary hosts, 2) route long-context requests to the hosted fallback model variant until we patch, or 3) apply egress shaping and conservative batching to reduce pressure. we probably need a combination. thoughts?
[02:07] Priya Sharma: rolling back is safer short term, but we need a playbook. also, we prefer not to route PHI traffic off our VPC to hosted tier for compliance reasons, so the fallback routing is tricky unless we can guarantee data residency.
[02:26] Marco Diaz: noted. we have a private fallback policy that can keep data in your VPC by pinning to a private model variant on different nodes, that avoids crossing your egress boundary. that's what we meant by 'hosted fallback' earlier, sorry if terminology was fuzzy.
[02:40] Priya Sharma: ok that helps, terminology is important. ethan, do you have capacity to accept routing to a different private node pool?
[02:49] Ethan Cole: yes, we can add a node group, but we want limits on bursting. also need to understand the egress shape - if that second pool sees the same kernel upgrade it's a non-solution.
[03:01] Marco Diaz: absolutely. plan is to route to nodes still on v1.12.2 which didn't get the patch, that's the canary fallback. for burst control we can apply per-customer token caps and a burst window.
[03:14] Marta Ruiz: we also need to confirm audit logs capture the route change and are stored in your customer-facing audit export. last time the mapping was ambiguous.
[03:24] Lena Park: action: marco to add audit-tag headers for any route shift so exports show before/after. will note that in the playbook.
[03:32] Marco Diaz: noted, i'll add header X-Redwood-Route-Prev and X-Redwood-Route-New to the logs.
[03:40] Priya Sharma: what's the expected impact to latency if we do the fallback to older nodes? any regression risk?
[03:47] Marco Diaz: older nodes run the older kernel which we validated in internal load tests — p95 should go back to baseline, maybe slight jitter during routing, but under 100ms for most calls. the main risk is capacity hit while the second pool warms up—prefix cache miss rate will be higher initially.
[04:05] Ethan Cole: warming is the thing i've been worried about. our Production traffic has big temporal locality, but the canary nodes are cold for some of our prompts. can we start with a small % of requests and ramp?
[04:16] Lena Park: yes canary ramp plan: 5% for 2 hours, 20% for 6 hours, then 50% if metrics look good. manual stop if p95 exceeds 150ms or error rate increases by >0.5%.
[04:30] Priya Sharma: good. on the kernel side, can you walk us through the rollback steps and risks? i'm asking because our infra team wants to be able to trigger it without needing to open tickets.
[04:41] Marco Diaz: rollback is fairly standard but we will provide a one-page checklist. steps: drain pool, apply kernel downgrade, restart agent, health-check KV cache priming. risk: brief outage during drain (~2-3 minutes per host), and potential for cold cache latencies post-restart. backup snapshot of configs recommended.
[05:00] Ethan Cole: that's acceptable, as long as we have the playbook and a button we can press in our runbook.
[05:08] Marta Ruiz: i want to confirm retention & encryption: when you do a route shift within our VPC, do any prompts ever leave our egress? we need to be crystal that nothing crosses region boundary.
[05:21] Marco Diaz: for your Private deployment, no prompt payloads will leave the VPC. the routing stays in-region and we preserve KMS-managed encryption. we can add an additional attestation in the telemetry export for the region and VPC id.
[05:35] Priya Sharma: good. also, can you provide a timeline for a patched kernel release that addresses the scheduling interaction?
[05:44] Marco Diaz: our runtime eng team identified the problematic scheduling patch and has a mitigated build in test. earliest safe delta build is target by 2027-02-28, with candidate validation on 2027-03-01. we'll prefer the rollback+canary then apply mitigated patch to canary nodes.
[06:00] Lena Park: sounds reasonable. switching topics briefly — egress shaping. Ethan, you mentioned retransmits earlier. we think shaping burst egress with token-level caps and a leaky-bucket for the node pool reduced retransmits. is that something you can deploy?
[06:18] Ethan Cole: we can. we'll need guidance on what thresholds to set. what does Redwood recommend for the leaky-bucket rate given our current p50 token throughput?
[06:27] Marco Diaz: looking at the sample, i'd recommend starting with a sustained rate equal to 1.2x your current p50 and a burst bucket sized for ~30 seconds of peak. i'll share a spreadsheet with the derived numbers but as a starting point for you: sustained 12k tokens/sec, burst 360k tokens.
[06:47] Priya Sharma: that spreadsheet will be helpful. also we want to avoid throttling that increases user-side timeouts leading to aborted requests. can you instrument graceful 429s vs queueing?
[06:58] Marco Diaz: yes, we support queueing with max wait time and will emit a queueing_hint header so you can monitor client timeouts. we'll set default max wait 200ms for now.
[07:12] Marta Ruiz: related security ask — when you do queueing or route changes, what audit metadata is captured? timestamps, previous route, user id, request hash?
[07:23] Marco Diaz: we capture timestamp, route id, route prev, model id, anonymized request fingerprint (not raw prompt), and the customer request id if supplied. we can also optionally include a SHA256 of the prompt if you want a verifiable hash.
[07:39] Priya Sharma: good, that'll satisfy our audit team for a first pass. can we pivot to telemetry thresholds you suggest to auto-fail a canary ramp? specifics please.
[07:51] Marco Diaz: auto-fail triggers: p95 increase > 20% vs baseline for 15 minutes, error rate increase > 0.5% absolute, and KV cache miss delta > 12% sustained. we can also add a manual stop.
[08:07] Ethan Cole: are these thresholds configurable from our console?
[08:12] Lena Park: yes, all thresholds are editable and we can pre-populate recommended defaults for the pilot.
[08:20] Priya Sharma: ok. one more item — quantization compatibility. we had flagged that the new kernel had an interaction with quantized kernels for the 4-bit variant, any update?
[08:31] Marco Diaz: good callout — the schedule jitter amplified memory reads for the int4 execute path leading to occasional outlier latencies. mitigated build includes a micro-scheduler patch that smooths jitter and adjusts prefetch timing. we'll validate with your quantized model on 2027-03-01.
[08:49] Marta Ruiz: do we need to re-run our quality evals after patch? our clinical team will want to verify summary fidelity didn't change.
[08:58] Marco Diaz: yes, we recommend running a small eval set (50 prompts) against the canary after deploy; we can automate that and surface diff metrics.
[09:09] Priya Sharma: perfect. downtime windows — when would you apply mitigated patch to full pool if canary looks good?
[09:17] Marco Diaz: earliest full pool rollout would be 2027-03-03 during your low-traffic window. final decision will hinge on canary telemetry and the eval diffs.
[09:27] Ethan Cole: sounds fine. on the operational side, would a soft-swap be possible? i.e., new nodes provisioned with mitigated kernel, warm cache using replay, then cutover.
[09:39] Marco Diaz: yes that's our preferred approach for minimal impact — provision, replay to warm KV cache, then cut traffic. we'll provide replay tooling for your infra.
[09:49] Lena Park: i'll note replay tooling as an action. marco will share runbook for replay.
[09:55] Priya Sharma: another ask from procurement: we need a short note on SLA impacts during rollback or canary failure events, specifically financial credits or do-nothing windows.
[10:07] Lena Park: i'll coordinate with our account team and legal to provide a note on how we treat SLA windows during maintenance—expect a follow-up by Friday.
[10:16] Marta Ruiz: on compliance, one more question — if you do a rollback, will change control be visible in our audit export with user id who initiated?
[10:25] Marco Diaz: yes, we'll include operator id and a change ticket id in the telemetry for every manual invokation.
[10:33] Priya Sharma: ok good. any blockers from Redwood side to do the canary tomorrow?
[10:38] Marco Diaz: none. we just need your node target group and permission to tag the canary nodes.
[10:45] Ethan Cole: i'll provide node group identifiers and will prepare IAM roles for tagging.
[10:51] Lena Park: timeline recap: Marco ships rollback playbook by 2027-02-25, Ethan shares egress metrics by 2027-02-28, Redwood provides mitigated build candidate 2027-02-28, canary bench 2027-03-01, replay tooling + eval automation before 2027-03-03 if canary OK.
[11:10] Priya Sharma: that matches our expectations. one last thing — potential competitive angle: if we hit too many interruptions we could look at Bedrock or running a hybrid with Anthropic for low-latency tail calls. not saying we'll switch but should be a consideration.
[11:27] Lena Park: understood, appreciate the candidness. we'll aim to reduce risk and share the runbooks.
[11:33] Marco Diaz: quick note on observability: we'll add a per-route heatmap to your console, showing KV cache hit, p95, and route id. that'll help you identify problematic prompts.
[11:44] Priya Sharma: yeah heatmap would help. please include correlation with request hashes so we can map to our feature flags.
[11:52] Marco Diaz: noted.
[11:55] Lena Park: ok wrapping — recap of action items and owners in the chat, can everyone confirm?
[12:02] Ethan Cole: confirmed.
[12:04] Marta Ruiz: confirmed.
[12:05] Priya Sharma: confirmed.
[12:07] Lena Park: thanks all, i'll send calendar invite for the canary readiness call next Monday 2027-03-01 14:00 UTC and attach the playbook. if anything urgent ping me or marco.
[12:18] (meeting ends)
